title: sed -i edits a .bashrc in a fake home
threat_model: No attacker. A user edits their own .bashrc in place with sed -i.
notes: setup.sh creates a fake home directly under /home with a .bashrc of a few lines before the pipeline starts. Predicted: no alert, because sed opens the original read-only, which the kernel filter skips, and GNU sed is expected to write a temporary file with another name and rename it, and rename is not hooked. The filter part is read from the code. How sed orders its syscalls is not checked, so this prediction is unsure and needs a live run.
